units.text: By whom impelled soars forth the mind projected? By whom enjoined goes forth the earliest breathing? By whom impelled this speech do people utter? The eye, the ear— what god, pray, them enjoineth? The all-conditioning, yet inscrutable agent, Brahma [Answer:]

That which is the hearing of the ear, the thought of the mind The voice of speech, as also the breathing of the breath, And the sight of the eyel Past these escaping, the wise, On departing from this world, become immortal.

There the eye goes not; Speech goes not, nor the mind. We know not, we understand not How one would teach It. Other, indeed, is It than the known, And moreover above the unknown. — Thus have we heard of the ancients {piirva) Who to us have explained It, This name of the Upanishad is taken from its first word J:ma, by whom. It is also known as the Talavakara, the name of the Brahmana of the Sama-Veda
That which is unexpressed with speech (tw, voice)j That with which speech is expressed— That indeed know as Brahma, Not this that people worship as this.

That which one breathes {praniti) not with breathing {pram, breath), [or, That which breathes not with breath,]' That with which breathing {prana) is conducted {pranlyati) — That indeed know as Brahma, Not this that people worship as this.
